skill.name: new-term-radar
skill.description: Discover new AI names and prioritize related keywords using the external new-term-radar CLI. Includes supplied-name research and complaint analysis, with required AIsa authentication.
skill.summary: Turn recent AI signals, supplied names, and tool complaints into keyword priorities with evidence and caveats.
skill.author: zhuyansen

security_audit.summary: All 42 static alerts are false positives: Markdown formatting, documented service authentication, public links, and research terminology explain the matches. No evidence found of credential theft, host reconnaissance, or prompt injection in the supplied instructions. A separate medium-risk concern remains: setup clones an unpinned external repository and executes its unaudited code with access to configured credentials.

remediation.issue: Setup executes an external repository without a pinned revision or integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed commit, verify the checkout, and obtain approval before downloading or executing code. Isolate execution and expose only required credentials.

content.user_title: Discover New AI Terms and Prioritize Keywords
content.value_statement: New AI names appear quickly, while demand signals remain incomplete and delayed. This skill guides CLI research into keyword priorities with source evidence and explicit caveats.
actual_capabilities: Guides daily collection of AI names from configured X accounts, GitHub breakouts, and new sitemap pages through an external CLI.
Supports keyword research for up to eight supplied names without running daily collection.
Organizes name and generic keywords by estimated demand, trend direction, competition, and prioritize, watch, or skip decisions.
Guides complaint research using Reddit, tutorial comments, and Chrome Web Store reviews when optional authentication is available.
Presents long-tail phrases, related names, brand flags, and source failures alongside recommendations.
Supports optional weekly demand signals, payment-link discovery, and authenticated TrustMRR revenue research.
limitations: Only instructions are bundled; execution requires an external repository, Python 3.10 or newer, AIsa authentication, and paid service calls.
The first daily run mainly builds snapshots, and immediate reruns report only changes since the previous run.
Search volume can lag about two months; daily estimates and worldwide trend readings are approximate.
Optional keys limit coverage; complaint research excludes App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot, Facebook groups, and There is An AI For That.

use_cases.title: Prioritize New AI Search Topics
use_cases.description: Compare recent AI names and related generic phrases before choosing pages to research or publish.

use_cases.title: Investigate Tool Complaints
use_cases.description: Review complaint themes, supporting quotes, and associated search phrases before selecting a product improvement.

use_cases.title: Track Emerging AI Releases
use_cases.description: Summarize new names from configured sources with links, signal strength, and collection caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Research One Known Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [AI product name] without daily collection. State estimated cost and duration first. Include demand, competition, brand flags, and missing-source caveats.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: compare keywords for a supplied name.

prompt_templates.title: Review Today's New Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my reviewed radar checkout to find today's new AI names. State cost and duration first. Include priorities, evidence links, and first-run limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: collect and prioritize recent signals.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Complaint Themes
prompt_templates.prompt: Research complaints about [tool category]. State estimated cost first. Group gaps by type with quotes, links, counts, and search phrases. Disclose unavailable sources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect user complaints to research opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [up to eight names] in one call. State cost first. Compare name and generic phrases, trend geography, competition, long tails, and source failures. Recommend follow-up checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare opportunities using several evidence types.

output_examples.input: What should I conclude from my first daily run if it finds few names?
output_examples.output: This run mainly established snapshots. Few results do not establish low activity. Review available GitHub breakouts and compare with a later run.

output_examples.input: How should I interpret a flat keyword trend without country-specific data?
output_examples.output: No rise was seen in the available worldwide series. The latest two days were excluded, so a recent increase may be missing.

output_examples.input: Can I treat complaint counts as market size?
output_examples.output: No. Counts describe the material read, not the entire market. Review linked quotes and source coverage before deciding what to build.

best_practices: Approve a reviewed, pinned radar checkout before execution, and keep API credentials out of prompts and published reports.
Review estimated cost and duration before each run, and avoid immediate daily reruns that change the comparison baseline.
Keep evidence links, source errors, first-run caveats, and volume delays visible when comparing recommendations.
anti_patterns: Treating missing data or a first-run snapshot as proof that demand is absent.
Publishing TrustMRR product lists despite the documented restriction on republication.
Inventing names, volumes, dates, or recommendations unsupported by the radar output.

faq.question: What must be available before running the skill?
faq.answer: A reviewed new-term-radar checkout, Python 3.10 or newer, and AIsa authentication are required. The supplied skill does not include the runtime.

faq.question: Can I research names I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. The keywords workflow skips collection and accepts up to eight names in one call.

faq.question: How much does research cost?
faq.answer: The instructions estimate daily research at about $0.30. Supplied-name research costs about $0.05 per name plus $0.09 per call. Optional signals add charges.

faq.question: Why does the first daily run show few results?
faq.answer: It primarily builds snapshots and reports GitHub breakouts. Later runs can compare source changes against those snapshots.

faq.question: Are GoAnyAPI and TrustMRR keys required?
faq.answer: No. GoAnyAPI enables related-search, country trend, and Chrome review features. TrustMRR enables optional revenue research with restrictions on republishing its data.

faq.question: Do search estimates prove an opportunity is profitable?
faq.answer: No. Estimates are approximate and delayed. Payment links show that a site sells something, not that it sells well.
